import FormalConjecturesUtil

import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«961»

/-!
# Erdős Problem 683

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/683](https://www.erdosproblems.com/683)
- [Er34] Erdős, Paul, A Theorem of Sylvester and Schur. J. London Math. Soc. (1934), 282--288.
- [Er55d] Erdős, P., On consecutive integers. Nieuw Arch. Wisk. (3) (1955), 124--128.
- [Er79d] Erdős, P., Some unconventional problems in number theory. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1979), 71-80.
-/

namespace Erdos683

open Filter Real Erdos961

/--
Let $P(n, k)$ be the largest prime factor of $\binom{n}{k}$.
-/
def P (n k : ℕ) : ℕ := (n.choose k).primeFactors.sup id

/--
Let $P(n, k)$ be the largest prime factor of $\binom{n}{k}$.
There exists $c > 0$ such that $P(n, k) \ge k^{1 + c}$ for all $0 < k \le n/2$.

Erdős originally stated this for $1 \le k \le n$ with a $\min(n-k+1, k^{1+c})$ bound [Er79d],
but as discussed on [erdosproblems.com](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/discuss/683),
the $\min$ term was introduced only to handle $k > n/2$; the problem is naturally stated
for $k \le n/2$ (cf. [#961](https://www.erdosproblems.com/961)).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_683 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n / 2 → (P n k : ℝ) ≥ k ^ (1 + c) := by
  sorry

/--
Sylvester and Schur [Er34] proved that $P(n, k) > k$ for $k \le n/2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_683.variant.sylvester_schur :
    ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n / 2 → P n k > k := by
  sorry

/--
Erdos [Er55d] improved this to $P(n, k) \gg k \log k $ for $k \le n/2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_683.variant.erdos_log :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n / 2 → P n k > c * k * Real.log k := by
  sorry

/--
Standard heuristics suggest that $P(n, k) > e^{c\sqrt{k}}$ for some constant $c > 0$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_683.variant.exp_sqrt :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n / 2 → P n k > Real.exp (c * Real.sqrt k) := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Erdos 683 and 961 are equivalent.

end Erdos683

findings.description: The lower bound omits the essential minimum with n - k + 1. Restricting to k ≤ n/2 does not make this term redundant: n = 2*k is permitted, and every prime divisor of choose (2*k) k is at most 2*k. For every c > 0, k^(1+c) eventually exceeds 2*k, so the entire right-hand side of this yes/no question is false. The docstring's justification for deleting the minimum is therefore incorrect. I proved the negation of the right-hand side in scratch Lean without using any sorry-backed theorem.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/683 asks whether P(binomial(n,k)) ≥ min(n-k+1, k^(1+c)) for some c > 0. Erdős, [Er79d], p.74, equation (6), also retains this minimum: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-23.pdf. The cited forum comment recommends restricting to k ≤ n/2, but the central-binomial case shows that this does not justify deleting the minimum.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the existing range, but replace the conclusion by `(P n k : ℝ) ≥ min (↑(n - k + 1) : ℝ) ((k : ℝ) ^ (1 + c))`, and correct the docstring accordingly. Restricting the original nondegenerate problem to this half-range is legitimate by binomial symmetry and Sylvester–Schur; deleting the minimum is not.

findings.description: The asserted uniform bound P(n,k) > c*k*log k under only 0 < k ≤ n/2 is false. Taking n = 2*k gives P(n,k) ≤ 2*k, whereas c*k*log k > 2*k for sufficiently large k, for every c > 0. The cited 1955 theorem requires the consecutive integers to exceed the prime threshold; that restriction has been lost in the binomial formulation. The same erroneous uncapped formula appears in the secondary website summary, so this is an inherited source-summary error, not merely a disagreement with the docstring. The negation of this Lean statement was proved independently of all problem sorries.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős, On consecutive integers [Er55d], p.124, defines f(K) using runs of integers each greater than K and proves in Theorem 1 that f(K) < C*K/log K: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1955-04.pdf. This does not give an uncapped k*log k lower bound when the run starts as low as k+1. The corresponding run-length statement is also recorded at https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/961.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the missing size qualification. A valid binomial consequence of [Er55d] is `∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n / 2 → (P n k : ℝ) ≥ min (↑(n - k + 1) : ℝ) (c * k * Real.log k)`. Alternatively, state the original run-length bound using `Erdos961.f`. Update the docstring to match.

findings.description: This also drops the minimum present in the primary source. For n = 2*k, P(n,k) ≤ 2*k, but exp(c*sqrt k) eventually exceeds 2*k for every positive c. Thus the stated existential assertion is false, not the intended exponential heuristic. Although the website summary reproduces this uncapped formula, Erdős's original formulation does not. I proved the negation in Lean using k = j^2 and n = 2*j^2, with no dependence on sorry.
findings.source_evidence: In [Er79d], p.74, immediately after equation (6), the Cramér-based heuristic has the form P(binomial(n,k)) > min{n-k+1, exp((1-ε)*sqrt k)}, with small values excepted: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-23.pdf. The minimum is absent from the summary at https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/683 and from this Lean declaration.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the capped exponential lower bound, replacing the conclusion by `(P n k : ℝ) > min (↑(n - k + 1) : ℝ) (Real.exp (c * Real.sqrt k))`, and update the docstring. For this existential-c version, finitely many small k can be accommodated by decreasing c; alternatively retain an explicit sufficiently-large-k qualification as in the primary source.

reformulations.difference: The classical consecutive-integer formulation in [Er34] is expressed as a largest-prime-factor statement about a binomial coefficient.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a block m, …, m+k-1 with m > k, put n = m+k-1; then 2*k ≤ n. Its product is k! * binomial(n,k). A prime p > k cannot divide k!, so such a prime divides the block product exactly when it divides the binomial coefficient. Conversely, n ≥ 2*k gives a block beginning at m = n-k+1 > k. The finite supremum defining P exceeds k exactly when there is a prime divisor exceeding k. The equivalence with the block-product formulation is proved as `sylvester_reformulation` in the scratch file.

sources_consulted: Erdős, A Theorem of Sylvester and Schur [Er34], especially the opening statement, https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1934-01.pdf
Erdős, On consecutive integers [Er55d], especially pp.124–125 and Theorem 1, https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1955-04.pdf
Erdős, Some unconventional problems in number theory [Er79d], especially p.74, https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-23.pdf
Local repository guidance: STATEMENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and AGENTS.md.
Local historical calibration: /workspace/past_misformalizations/INDEX.md, pr01711.md, pr01532.md, pr01526.md, pr01388.md, and pr03884.md.
review.notes: All five declarations were checked. `P` returns 0 when the binomial coefficient is 0 or 1, but the theorem hypotheses force the coefficient to exceed 1, so this default causes no defect. Natural-number division in the half-range is equivalent to 2*k ≤ n. Small inputs were evaluated, and /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully. It proves `P_le_n`, the negations of all three uncapped bounds, and the Sylvester–Schur reformulation; their axiom reports contain no sorryAx. The website's inaccurate summaries of the two variants were checked against the primary papers rather than treated as independent evidence. These are statement errors, not stale-status reports. The reviewed repository file was not modified.

submission.summary: Restored the minimum with n - k + 1 in all three lower bounds, using the non-strict capped logarithmic bound. Updated their docstrings to match the primary sources and corrected the explanation of the half-range restriction. Other declarations and category attributes were left unchanged. The required compile command succeeds with only expected `sorry` warnings.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«961»

/-!
# Erdős Problem 683

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/683](https://www.erdosproblems.com/683)
- [Er34] Erdős, Paul, A Theorem of Sylvester and Schur. J. London Math. Soc. (1934), 282--288.
- [Er55d] Erdős, P., On consecutive integers. Nieuw Arch. Wisk. (3) (1955), 124--128.
- [Er79d] Erdős, P., Some unconventional problems in number theory. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1979), 71-80.
-/

namespace Erdos683

open Filter Real Erdos961

/--
Let $P(n, k)$ be the largest prime factor of $\binom{n}{k}$.
-/
def P (n k : ℕ) : ℕ := (n.choose k).primeFactors.sup id

/--
Let $P(n, k)$ be the largest prime factor of $\binom{n}{k}$.
Is there a constant $c > 0$ such that
$P(n, k) \ge \min(n-k+1, k^{1+c})$ for all $0 < k \le n/2$?

Erdős posed this bound in [Er79d]. For $n/2 < k < n$, it follows from binomial
symmetry and the Sylvester--Schur theorem. The minimum is still necessary in
the range $k \le n/2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_683 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n / 2 →
      (P n k : ℝ) ≥ min (↑(n - k + 1) : ℝ) ((k : ℝ) ^ (1 + c)) := by
  sorry

/--
Sylvester and Schur [Er34] proved that $P(n, k) > k$ for $k \le n/2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_683.variant.sylvester_schur :
    ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n / 2 → P n k > k := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős's bound [Er55d] on consecutive integers implies that there exists $c > 0$
such that $P(n, k) \ge \min(n-k+1, c k \log k)$ for all $0 < k \le n/2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_683.variant.erdos_log :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n / 2 →
      (P n k : ℝ) ≥ min (↑(n - k + 1) : ℝ) (c * k * Real.log k) := by
  sorry

/--
Standard heuristics on prime gaps [Er79d] suggest that
$P(n, k) > \min(n-k+1, e^{c\sqrt{k}})$ for some constant $c > 0$ and all
$0 < k \le n/2$.

Since the constant is unspecified, the small values excluded in [Er79d] can
be covered by decreasing $c$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_683.variant.exp_sqrt :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n / 2 →
      (P n k : ℝ) > min (↑(n - k + 1) : ℝ) (Real.exp (c * Real.sqrt k)) := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Erdos 683 and 961 are equivalent.

end Erdos683
